executive_assessment.text: Named Rendova communities and provincial water investments add local vulnerability and governance detail; project surveys and two-community fieldwork are not representative rankings.

A historical Honiara disaster-recovery grievance case illustrates a possible mechanism, but the same three-country study finds no significant aggregate disaster/temperature association with social conflict.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2020-10-26 reports: The 2015-16 El Niño drought affected Central, Rennell and Bellona, and Temotu; schools closed and communities prioritized water projects.
Source dated 2020-10-26 reports: Over 80 percent of CRISP subprojects involved water, mainly rainwater harvesting; dry-season shortages made it a priority in Malaita, Rennell and Central.
Source dated 2020-10-26 reports: Tulagi's 260-metre shoreline works protected the road and foreshore trees during Tropical Cyclone Harold in April 2020.
Source dated 2020 reports: Baniata had 533 residents and eight-community Lokuru had 1,065; households relied on gardens, fisheries, forest nuts and groundwater for food and livelihoods.

Source dated 2020 reports: Both sites identified gardens, reefs and fish, water, rivers, shorelines and low-lying infrastructure as vulnerable; factors included hazard exposure, high dependence and weak resource management.

Source dated 2020 reports: Workshops used local coordinators and women's and men's groups; priorities included leadership, health, farming, livelihood diversification, resource management and youth capacity.
Source dated 2020 reports: Participants said cultural change and weaker local governance reduced use of traditional tabu areas; they proposed a community marine protected area and fisheries rules.

Source dated 2026-01-22 reports: The authors describe an event in which people displaced by April 2014 floods to a Honiara informal settlement protested and rioted on 16 May, perceiving the government rehabilitation package as inadequate for their disaster losses.

Source dated 2026-08-25 reports: UNDP reports an expanded agroforestry nursery in West Kwarae, mangrove rehabilitation and a community centre in South Malaita, reforestation in West Are'are, and land restoration improving student access at Afio Primary School.

Source dated 2026-08-25 reports: UNDP reports that the Wahere Community Association built a seawall at Marau Sound, East Guadalcanal, to protect homes, infrastructure and livelihoods from coastal erosion and rising sea levels.

Source dated 2026-10-20 reports: The government reports that the NAP was under formulation in October 2026, drawing on a 12-sector CRVA with consultations in all nine provinces and SIIVA assessments in Isabel and Makira focused on daily climate and livelihood effects.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 21 of 21 evidence records and 2 of 2 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No countrywide causal estimate of climate impacts on conflict or violence is established by these sources.
Full subnational coverage and independently evaluated long-term response effectiveness remain gaps.
Full underlying community datasets and current provincial conflict incidence were not inspected.

National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Selected-site relocation and land-access mechanism is conditional, without national causal attribution.
The evidence is site- and project-specific; it does not provide a comprehensive current vulnerability ranking across provinces or province-level conflict incidence.

The 2026 climate-conflict study reports one Honiara post-flood protest-turned-riot but finds no statistically significant aggregate disaster or temperature effect for its three-country panel; the event mechanism was not statistically tested.

No source located in the targeted searches showed insecurity or organized violence interrupting a named climate-adaptation delivery operation; no such reverse pathway is inferred from historical unrest.

The CRISP ICR survey was non-representative and excluded Rennell and Bellona; the Western Province study purposively selected two communities and its adaptation-plan implementation required subsequent monitoring.

The 2026 CRVA story map did not render substantive text in direct access, the 2025 South Malaita ESRAM download failed, and the 2019 State of Environment PDF returned 403. Their findings are not used here.
The SAGE study's Methods specify 2012-2020, while Discussion mentions13years/936observations. This inconsistency is flagged rather than silently reconciled.
The coordinator could not reopen the government NAP endpoint; its bounded planning claims rely on the collector's original-page extraction.
The World Bank ICR bears a public-disclosure-authorization stamp; no restricted-only document is reproduced.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
